verdict.rationale: Google's support docs give a clear lost-phone recovery path: codes sync to your Google Account and are automatically restored when you sign in to Authenticator on a new device. The manual QR transfer needs the old device, so it does not cover a lost phone. Community complaints about tokens being lost mostly describe the era before cloud sync or the phone's own OS backup, so they do not contradict the documented account sync. Missing for 10: hands-on or independent confirmation that a restore on a new device works, and any recovery option for people who use the app without a Google Account (the documented 'Use without an account' mode only supports transfer from the old device).

support.subject: As an everyday user, losing my phone doesn't lose my accounts — a documented recovery path restores my tokens on a new device

citations.quote: When you sign in to your Google Account within Google Authenticator on a new device, your codes are automatically synced to this device.
With Google Authenticator, you can synchronize your verification codes across all your devices, simply by signing in to your Google Account.
This helps protect you from being locked out of your account when you change devices.
